sections.heading: Build a clear sales process for agency growth, retainers and better client relationships

items.html: Build a clear sales process for agency growth, retainers and better client relationships

Marketing and digital agency sales is not just about collecting leads and sending proposals. A new opportunity may become a discovery call, a creative brief, a strategy discussion, a project proposal, a monthly retainer, a campaign, a website project, a performance marketing engagement or a long-term client relationship.

The challenge is that many agencies still manage sales across spreadsheets, inboxes, calendars, proposal documents, project tools, Slack messages and individual memory. That makes it difficult to answer important sales questions.

● Which leads are qualified?
● Which briefs are complete?
● Which proposals are waiting for follow-up?
● Which opportunities are stuck because of budget, scope or decision delay?
● Which projects could become retainers?
● Which existing clients are ready for upsell or account growth?
● Which client conversations should be summarized before the next call?

I help marketing and digital agencies build a clear, practical and AI-ready sales process in Pipedrive – a CRM built by salespeople, for salespeople.

With the right setup, your agency can manage leads, discovery calls, briefs, proposals, retainers, project handovers, account growth, sales performance and AI-supported sales insights in one structured system.

sections.heading: Why agency sales becomes hard to manage

items.html: Why agency sales becomes hard to manage

Marketing and digital agencies usually work with many different opportunity types at the same time. You may sell strategy projects, branding, website development, SEO, paid media, social media management, marketing automation, creative campaigns, content services, analytics, consulting or monthly retainers.

Some prospects need a one-time project. Some need ongoing support. Some are not ready yet. Some want a proposal before the brief is clear. Some are a good fit strategically, but not commercially. Without a clear CRM process, the same problems appear again and again.

Leads are not qualified properly

Not every lead is a good agency opportunity. Some prospects have no budget. Some are not ready to start. Some do not know what they need. Some want a full strategy for free before making a decision. If qualification is not structured, the agency spends time on the wrong opportunities and misses better ones.

Briefs are incomplete

In agency sales, a good proposal starts with a good brief. If the brief is unclear, the proposal becomes vague, pricing becomes risky and delivery expectations become harder to manage.

Proposals disappear after they are sent

Sending a proposal is not the end of the sales process. The prospect may compare agencies, discuss internally, change scope, delay the project, ask for revisions or wait for budget approval. If follow-up is not scheduled properly, strong opportunities can go silent.

Project and retainer opportunities are mixed together

A one-time website project and a long-term paid media retainer are very different sales opportunities. If your pipeline treats every deal the same way, it becomes difficult to forecast revenue, plan capacity and prioritize the best opportunities.

Scope creep starts before the deal is even won

Agency scope problems often begin during sales. If the team does not capture what is included, what is excluded, what success means, how many revision rounds are expected or what input the client must provide, delivery can start with confusion.

Sales-to-delivery handover is weak

When a deal is won, the delivery team needs clean information. If the handover is based on scattered notes or memory, the project can start with missing context: unclear scope, wrong expectations, weak brief, missing assets, unclear deadlines or undocumented promises.

Existing clients are not developed proactively

The best agency growth often comes from existing clients. A project client may become a retainer client. A social media client may need SEO. A website client may need conversion optimization. A campaign client may need marketing automation. If account growth opportunities are not tracked, the agency becomes reactive instead of proactive.

Long client conversations are hard to review

Agency sales often includes long email threads, brief discussions, proposal revisions, creative feedback, budget questions and several stakeholders. If this information is hard to summarize before the next follow-up, salespeople lose time and risk missing important details. This is where AI can help but only if the client history, deal data and sales process are properly structured.

sections.heading: How I would structure your agency sales process in Pipedrive

items.html: How I would structure your agency sales process in Pipedrive

When I implement Pipedrive for a marketing or digital agency, I do not start with software settings. I start with your real sales process.

● Where do leads come from?
● What makes a lead qualified?
● When do you book a discovery call?
● What information is needed before creating a proposal?
● How do you capture the brief?
● How do you separate project work from retainer opportunities?
● How do you follow up after sending a proposal?
● When does sales hand over to delivery?
● How do you track account growth and upsell?
● What does management need to see every week?
● What kind of sales data would make AI useful later?
Once this is clear, we can build a CRM setup that supports daily agency sales work.

A typical marketing and digital agency sales pipeline in Pipedrive could look like this:

1New lead received
2Initial qualification
3Discovery call scheduled
4Discovery completed
5Brief / requirements confirmed
6Proposal in preparation

The goal is simple: every opportunity should have a clear stage, a responsible owner, a next activity and useful data that can support better decisions later.
AI can only help if the sales process is clear enough to understand.

sections.heading: What Pipedrive helps you control in agency sales

items.html: What Pipedrive helps you control in agency sales
Lead and inquiry management

Pipedrive helps your agency capture and organize new leads, referral opportunities, inbound inquiries, consultation requests and campaign leads in one system. Instead of losing opportunities in emails, forms or spreadsheets, every potential client can be created, assigned, qualified and followed up.
Discovery and brief management

Your team can track important discovery details such as business goal, current marketing situation, target audience, budget, urgency, decision process, service interest and expected outcome. This helps the agency prepare better proposals and avoid vague scope.
Sales pipeline visibility

Your team and management can see where each opportunity stands: new lead, discovery, brief confirmed, proposal sent, negotiation, won or handover. This makes agency sales easier to manage because everyone works from the same view.
Proposal and contract workflow
Proposals, quotes, statements of work and agreements can be connected to the sales process. This makes it easier to track what was sent, when it was sent and what needs to happen next.
Retainer and project visibility

With the right setup, your agency can separate one-time projects from monthly retainers, pilot projects, campaign work and account growth opportunities. This helps with revenue forecasting and capacity planning.
Decision-maker visibility

Agency deals often involve founders, marketing managers, sales leaders, e-commerce managers, finance teams, procurement, brand managers or external advisors. Pipedrive helps you keep these contacts connected to the right deal or account.
Sales-to-delivery handover

A won deal should not become a messy handover. Pipedrive can help keep the final scope, brief, proposal, timeline, expectations, assets, decision-makers and next steps visible before the client moves into delivery.
Account growth and upsell visibility
With the right setup, your team can track existing clients, retainer renewal, upsell potential, cross-sell opportunities, account reviews and referral opportunities.
Reporting and forecasting

With the right pipeline stages, fields and dashboards, you can track open opportunities, proposal conversion, retainer pipeline, project pipeline, source performance, stuck deals, lost reasons, sales activity and account growth potential.
Automation

Repetitive tasks can be automated. For example, when a proposal is sent, Pipedrive can create a follow-up activity. When a deal is won, it can trigger a handover task for the delivery team. When an account review is due, it can remind the account owner.
AI-supported sales work

AI becomes useful when your CRM data is clean. In agency sales, your team may handle many discovery notes, client briefs, proposal revisions, creative discussions, budget questions and follow-ups at the same time.

Pipedrive’s AI tools can support sales work by helping your team summarize client conversations, prepare follow-up emails, identify sales patterns and focus on opportunities that need attention.

For example, AI can help a salesperson quickly understand a long client email thread before replying. It can also help managers prepare pipeline reviews by identifying proposals without next activities, slow-moving opportunities, repeated lost reasons or clients that may be ready for upsell.

The goal is to help your team spend less time searching for information and more time winning better-fit clients, improving proposals and growing accounts.

sections.heading: Practical CRM habits for marketing and digital agencies

items.html: Practical CRM habits for marketing and digital agencies

Never treat every lead as a good agency fit. A lead is not automatically worth a proposal. Track budget, urgency, decision process, service need, internal readiness and strategic fit before investing too much time.

Structure every discovery call. A good discovery call should capture the client’s business goal, current situation, target audience, problem, decision-makers, timeline, budget and next step. This makes proposals much stronger.

Do not create a proposal before the brief is clear. A vague brief creates vague pricing and delivery risk. Before proposal stage, make sure the business goal, scope, deliverables and success criteria are clear enough.

Never send a proposal without a follow-up activity. A proposal without a planned follow-up is a risk. Every proposal should have a scheduled call, email or next action.

Separate project work from retainers. A website project, a campaign and a monthly retainer should not be managed exactly the same way. Use pipelines, labels or custom fields to make the difference visible.

Track scope clearly. Agency projects can become unprofitable when scope is unclear. Track what is included, what is excluded, what may change, what needs client input and what still needs clarification.

Make decision-makers visible. The person who fills out the form is not always the person who decides. Track the champion, decision-maker, finance contact, marketing owner, internal influencer and daily contact.

Prepare clean delivery handovers. The delivery team should not have to guess what was promised during sales. Track final scope, brief, timeline, assets, stakeholders, success criteria, risks and next steps before the deal is handed over.

Review account growth opportunities regularly. The first project should not be the end of the sales process. Track which clients could buy additional services, move into a retainer, renew a campaign, request strategy support or refer another client.

Keep client communication easy to summarize. If your team wants to use AI effectively, client history needs to be organized. Important emails, notes, calls, briefs, proposal versions, scope changes, creative feedback, next steps and decision-makers should be connected to the right deal or account. This makes AI-supported summaries, follow-up preparation and sales insights much more useful.

Use CRM data before using AI. AI will only help if the sales data is structured. First build a clean pipeline, clear qualification logic, useful client history, consistent activities, meaningful lost reasons and proper handover data. Then use AI to improve summaries, follow-up writing, prioritization and sales decisions.

sections.heading: Your project management tool manages delivery. Your CRM should manage opportunities and account growth.

items.html: Your project management tool manages delivery. Your CRM should manage opportunities and account growth.

Many marketing and digital agencies already use tools for project management, creative work, delivery, reporting, collaboration, time tracking or client communication. That is important but those tools are not the same as CRM. Your project management or delivery tools usually manage:
● tasks,
● timelines,
● creative production,
● campaign delivery,
● website development,
● client approvals,
● time tracking,
● reporting,
● internal collaboration,
● and project execution.

Your CRM should manage what happens before and around the commercial relationship:
● new leads,
● discovery calls,
● briefs,
● qualification,
● proposals,
● follow-ups,
● negotiations,
● decision-makers,
● lost reasons,
● forecast,
● sales-to-delivery handover,
● retainer opportunities,
● upsell, cross-sell,
● and account growth.

Pipedrive does not need to replace your project management or delivery systems. The goal is not to rebuild your agency operations. The goal is to create a clear sales layer before and around the client relationship, so your team can manage opportunities, follow-ups, handovers, retainers and account growth more effectively. This sales layer also creates the clean data foundation your team needs if you want to use AI in a practical way.

● Which discovery calls are scheduled?

● Which opportunities could become monthly retainers?

You can also use AI-supported insights to prepare better sales meetings. For example, your team can review:

● Which long client conversations should be summarized before follow-up?
● Which brief notes need to be turned into clear next steps?
● Which proposals may need a next activity?
● Which opportunities are moving too slowly?
● Which lost reasons appear repeatedly?
● Which lead sources produce better-fit clients?
● Which clients may be ready for retainer, upsell or cross-sell?
● Which service categories may need more sales focus?
● Which won deals may need cleaner delivery handover notes?

AI does not replace the sales meeting. It helps the team prepare faster and focus on the most important agency growth opportunities.

sections.heading: Is Pipedrive the right CRM for your agency?

items.html: Is Pipedrive the right CRM for your agency?

Pipedrive is a strong fit if your sales process includes:

● inbound leads or consultation requests,
● discovery calls,
● briefs,
● proposals or statements of work,
● project and retainer opportunities,
● multiple decision-makers,
● scope discussions,
● proposal revisions,
● sales-to-delivery handover,
● account reviews,
● upsell or cross-sell opportunities,
● and a need for better sales visibility.

Pipedrive is also a strong fit if you want to use AI in a practical way not as a buzzword, but as a tool to help your team summarize client conversations, prepare follow-ups, identify sales patterns and focus on the right opportunities.

AI works best when your sales process is already structured. That is why the first step is not AI. The first step is building a clean, usable agency sales process. If your team still manages opportunities in spreadsheets, inboxes, proposal documents or disconnected systems, Pipedrive can help you create a more structured and predictable sales operation.

The goal is to help your agency focus on better-fit clients, follow up at the right time, send stronger proposals and give leadership a clear view of the real sales pipeline.
Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

What is a CRM for marketing and digital agencies?

A CRM for marketing and digital agencies helps teams manage leads, discovery calls, briefs, proposals, follow-ups, contacts, sales activities, forecasts, delivery handovers, retainers and account growth opportunities in one system.

For agencies, CRM is especially useful because sales often involves unclear briefs, proposal revisions, multiple stakeholders, project-based revenue and long-term client growth potential.

Why do agencies need CRM if they already use project management tools?

Project management tools usually manage delivery after the client is won.

CRM manages the commercial process: leads, qualification, discovery, briefs, proposals, follow-ups, decision-makers, lost reasons, retainers and account growth.

Your project management tool helps you deliver client work. Your CRM helps you win and grow client relationships.

Can Pipedrive help manage agency proposals?

Yes. Pipedrive can help your team track proposal status, follow-up activities, proposal revisions, decision-makers and expected close dates.

With Smart Docs, proposals, quotes and agreements can be connected to the sales process.

Can Pipedrive help agencies sell more retainers?

Yes. You can track retainer potential, monthly revenue opportunities, account growth, renewal dates and upsell opportunities in Pipedrive.

This helps agencies separate one-time project work from recurring revenue opportunities.

Can Pipedrive help with sales-to-delivery handover?

Yes. Pipedrive can help keep the final brief, scope, deliverables, client expectations, timeline, notes and next steps visible before the client moves into delivery.

This helps reduce confusion after a deal is won.

Can Pipedrive help track lead sources?

Yes. You can track whether leads come from referrals, website forms, SEO, paid ads, LinkedIn outreach, events, partners, webinars or past clients.

This helps agency leaders understand which channels generate real sales opportunities, not just leads.

Can AI help agency sales teams?

Yes, but only when CRM data is structured.

Once client data, discovery notes, briefs, proposals, follow-ups and sales history are clean, AI can help summarize client conversations, support follow-up writing, identify sales patterns and help your team prioritize the right opportunities.

Can Pipedrive AI help with proposal follow-up emails?

Yes. Pipedrive’s AI email tools can help create sales emails and summarize long email conversations.

This is especially useful in agency sales, where client communication may include brief changes, creative feedback, budget questions, proposal revisions and several stakeholders.

The salesperson still controls the message. AI helps prepare faster.

Can Pipedrive AI help with account reviews?

Yes, if the data is clean.

AI-supported insights can help managers prepare account reviews by identifying clients without recent activity, slow-moving opportunities, repeated lost reasons, retainer potential or patterns in sales performance.

The account review still needs human judgment. AI simply helps the team focus on what matters.

Is Pipedrive difficult for agency teams to use?

Pipedrive is designed to be simple and visual.

However, CRM success does not only depend on the software. It depends on whether the sales process is set up correctly and whether the team understands how to use it in daily work.

That is why implementation and training are important.
